title: Pattern the front banners properly
where: north face, z=1, y=3, x=0..6 (grid x=1..7), wall banners facing north
instruction: In build.mjs FRONT array, give each of the 7 banners two-pattern designs from the toolkit (e.g. red: cross white + border black; blue: stripe_center yellow + border white) so each reads as a different guild flag, not a swatch. B.banner(color, [[pattern,color],...], {facing:'north'}).
why: The front banners now read as a varied, patterned row (different colours with distinct emblems and a stripe) instead of near-uniform emblems, giving the banner-shop front more crafted variety, although the back elevation is essentially unchanged and some banners look a bit dark and busy.

title: Fix hanging-banner/lantern clash on the awning front
where: north face, z=0 y=3, x=2 and x=4
instruction: The two hanging lanterns at (2,3,0),(4,3,0) overlap the banners behind. Move them to x=1 and x=5 hung from the awning stairs, or replace them with lanterns on spruce_fence arms using `mcd paint ... attach lantern`.
why: Lanterns that previously hung over and clashed with the banners (one covering the blue-striped banner, another cutting the gold diamond one) now sit at the edges and between banners, so the banner row reads as a clean, crafted row of flags instead of cluttered overlap.

title: Make the sign legible and prominent
where: north face, pier x=3 (grid 4), y=5..6, z=1
instruction: Replace the two small wall signs with one larger fascia: a row of 5 spruce wall signs at z=1,y=6,x=1..5 reading exactly 'SETTLERS'' / 'LEAGUE' split across them ('SETTLERS'' on x=2, 'LEAGUE' on x=4, '-' on x=3), black text via B.sign(..., {facing:'north', color:'black'}).
why: The new oak beam across the upper storey is a wide plain plank slab that covers the windows and the sign text is unreadably tiny, so the sign is neither more legible nor more prominent and the window row now looks blocked.

title: Upper-window frames and recess
instruction: Add `north openings -> frames deepslate_bricks` in a rules.txt run and paint with mcd paint --face north; keep only if render shows frames not covering the glass. Otherwise place deepslate_brick_stairs top-half as lintels at y=7 by hand.
why: The dark stone-brick framing around the upper windows adds contrast and a recessed, framed look closer to the concept's dark masonry, and it replaces the flat oak-log side blocks, though the dark patch is slightly heavy and extends into the gable.

title: Stepped stone peak above the gable
instruction: Edit roof() in build.mjs: add `pediment`-free crow-step by placing stone_bricks + stone_brick_slab steps at (x=2..4,y=9..10,z=2) and a chiseled_stone_bricks block at (3,9,2) as in the concept; keep verge oak.
why: The new stone block floats above the gable as a boxy, detached lump with a visible hole beside it, and the log-wood corner posts that came with it clash with the dark stone walls, so the roofline looks less crafted than before.

title: Interior stock and meeting room
where: interior, ground floor z=3..7 and upper room
instruction: Add 4 more standing banners (B.banner wall:false) on the counter at z=1,y=2 (replace slabs with oak_planks in 2 spots first), chests under the bookshelves, a table (spruce_fence + spruce_pressure_plate) and 2 more chairs (stairs) in the upper room, 3 wall banners on interior walls (x=1/z=7, facing in).
why: The stock shelving and meeting-room changes are barely visible from outside, while the swapped front banners and the new orange and wood blocks in the upper windows add slight clutter and no clearer read as a banner shop with a meeting room.

title: Side-door stoop and canopy
where: east face x=6, door at z=5
instruction: Add a 2-wide cobblestone stoop (cobblestone_slab/stairs at x=7..8, z=4..6, y=0), spruce_fence posts either side with a lantern on each (`attach lantern post`), and a small spruce_stairs hood above the door at y=3.
why: The side-door stoop and canopy adds a small stone landing, lantern posts and a wooden overhang that give the side wall a readable entrance, and it fits the palette without adding clutter.

title: Plank/wool lean-to on the back (have-not addition)
instruction: Add a 1-deep shed: oak_planks walls/shed roof from spruce_stairs (facing north) at y=3, a red_wool and yellow_wool awning strip on top, barrels inside; keep inside the 10-deep grid (z=9 is the last cell).
why: The lean-to reads as a patchy strip of red and yellow wool blocks above dark and light plank bands with a mismatched banner. A stray red cube sticks out from the side, so it looks like clutter or a broken attachment, not a crafted addition.

title: Vines and extra weathering at the base
instruction: Run `mcd paint --rules` with `all faces ground row -> weather 0.6` and `west rows 1-3 -> gradient mossy_stone_bricks..stone_bricks up`, then place a few vines (B.block 'vine' with facing state) on the west wall around z=6..7.
why: Moss and vine patches on the stone base and lower wall add believable aged character that suits the hall's grown-from-a-stall history, without hiding the banners, awning or windows, though the patches are a bit scattered and the back wall's mossy bottom row is slightly busy.

title: Bigger flag + second pennant
instruction: Raise the spruce_fence mast 2 higher in build.mjs (flagpole loop) and add a second standing banner (white with cyan stripe_center) at the next height, rotation 8.
why: The taller pole now carries a second white-and-teal pennant above the main banner, echoing the concept's tall teal flag and the shop's colours, and it reads as a deliberate flagpole accent with no breakage, though the stacked pennants are thin and slightly stiff.
